last_assistant_message:
Week-2.md rewrite complete. Report:

**Changes:**
- Replaced the 7 inlined "Starter Commands (RT-Only)" stubs with an orientation to the real DLP student workspace (`../AI-Deep-Learning-Program/student-workspace/`): `skills/` skeletons with frontmatter and File Contracts, `demo-outputs/`, `sample-stories/` trio, `schemas/`, `evaluations/`. Explicit framing: these are the same artifacts grads will coach in DLP Sessions 1-3.
- Replaced the `../Resources/SDLC-Workflow.png` reference with `../AI-Deep-Learning-Program/images/sdlc-pipeline.svg`, and redrew the inline mermaid diagram to show the YAML handoffs (`stories.yaml`, `plan.yaml`, code, `review.yaml`) including fail-fast notes and the review write-back edge.
- All Promptfoo content replaced with AI-written Python evaluation scripts: Monday afternoon is now "Baseline Evaluation for create-prd" (candidate writes EC by hand, AI writes the script, deterministic first / LLM judge second). All iteration loops, artifacts review, deliverables updated to match.
- Terminology swept: commands → skills, test criteria → EC (with an explicit EC vs AC callout Monday), Context = WHY / Constraints = HOW (Tuesday's Context-first block now teaches the intent-vs-rules distinction plus the "is this instruction in the right RTCC section?" diagnostic).
- Added the three-way quality-bar contrast exercise (good / vague / AI-generated sample stories) Monday afternoon as the EC-sharpening demo.
- Named the plan quality dependency explicitly in Thursday's plan-story block (code from the plan, never the story) plus the fail-fast contract and AC-coverage schema rule.
- Added the review feedback loop to Friday: review-implementation writes verdict/notes back into `stories.yaml`; deliverables now require a committed pipeline run showing the write-back.
- Coaching notes rewritten: new failure modes for "AI writes the EC" (inverts EDD) and "LLM judge for everything" (deterministic first); kept upstream tracing, audit enforcement, and ambiguity-in-inputs notes.

**Judgment calls:**
- Kept the H1 title's em-dash ("# AI Bootcamp — Week 2: ...") since it's the naming pattern across all four week files and @Overview; all body/heading/list em-dashes became colons per the canon rule.
- Assumed Week 1 introduces the Python eval pattern (per the parent's Week 1 fork scope), so Week 2 uses it without re-teaching setup.
- En-dashes retained in time ranges ("9:00 – 5:00"); the rule targets em-dashes.

**Out-of-scope note:** `Week-2.md` no longer references the bootcamp's own katas either; the katas decision belongs to the parent's cleanup pass.
